title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she used psychedelic mushrooms. She found the false statement in a letter sent to her GP after kidney stone surgery in March. Because she was receiving workers' compensation, she feared the error could hurt her case. After she complained, the urologist apologized, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

The article says about 40 percent of Australian GPs regularly use AI scribes, though none are approved by the medical device regulator. A privacy watchdog report found other serious mistakes, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis. The Therapeutic Goods Administration has been reviewing these tools and will release findings in the coming weeks, with breaches to be acted on. Patient advocates want approved lists and stronger checks, while Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already knows.
